title: How Does an Insect Keep Hiding as a Leaf for 47 Million Years?
subject: leaf insect

scenes.text: How does an insect hide in plain sight for 47 million years?
In Germany's Messel Pit, scientists found a fossil about six centimeters long. Its flat body matched leaves from the same rock.
It's called Eophyllium, the first fossil leaf insect ever found.
Reported in 2007, it was almost identical in body to leaf insects alive today.
Scientists called leaf imitation an ancient and successful strategy. No upgrade needed.
Forty-seven million years. Same trick. And it still works.

description:
A fossil leaf insect from Germany is about 47 million years old.
Eophyllium messelensis, found at Messel and described in 2007, already had a flat, leaf-shaped body, and its anatomy was close to modern leaf insects. Scientists say leaf imitation is an ancient and successful strategy.
Could you spot a leaf insect on a branch?
